statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete: all 58 registered checks have a conclusive outcome.

page.framework: server-rendered MPA with deferred JavaScript and ad/consent integrations
page.notes: Public live-score, match-detail, standings, and calendar templates. Homepage plus three distinct templates and a failure state were audited; other sport pages were excluded as template-equivalent.

checkOutcomes.method: evaluate probe and screenshot under prefers-color-scheme: dark
checkOutcomes.evidence: Computed colorScheme was normal and body remained rgb(255,255,255); CSS contained no prefers-color-scheme rule.
The page exposed no active animations, so there was no non-essential motion to suppress.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit and prefers-contrast screenshot
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found consent text contrast as low as 1.06:1, 1.82:1, and 2.8:1.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS and navigation inspection across list and detail routes
checkOutcomes.evidence: The MPA route changes are abrupt and CSS contains no view-transition declarations.
No scroll-linked animation, parallax, reveal, or scrollytelling interaction exists on the representative pages.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scroll-linked animation, parallax, reveal, or scrollytelling interaction exists on the representative pages.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The site exposes ordinary links only, with no gesture-driven control to evaluate.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site exposes ordinary links only, with no gesture-driven control to evaluate.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The 6,123px results page has no sticky context, progress indicator, or scroll-state-aware chrome.
No tooltip, menu, or popover overlay requiring anchored positioning was present.
checkOutcomes.reason: No tooltip, menu, or popover overlay requiring anchored positioning was present.

checkOutcomes.evidence: Score-only links open a new detail page abruptly and the Top links provide no transition or highlight cue.
A full-screen consent wall obscures all scores on every audited route before interaction.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM inspection of the consent overlay
checkOutcomes.evidence: The modal is a div with role=dialog rather than native dialog, while the page has zero dialog/popover/details elements.
Behind the consent layer, pages use compact navigation and devote most space to scores, match details, tables, or dates.
Home and match templates report 10px horizontal overflow at a 360px visual viewport; standings and calendar do not overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: CSS inspection and narrow layout comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS contains no @container rules; dense score rows retain tiny desktop-like text and targets on mobile.
Many links are only 12px high and score links are about 10x12px; the focused consent dialog had only a transparent outline.
The brand, sport/date/status filters, live scores, and REFRESH NOW action make the site purpose and next actions clear.
Score and Standings links resolve to populated detail and table pages with Back and Top recovery links.
The error page says the page cannot be displayed and to try later, has no title, and offers only a generic home link with no retry or cause.
Lighthouse measured LCP 5.5s and TTI 8.1s; the trace measured LCP 3.06s. CLS and TBT were good.
Observed CLS ranged from 0.052 to 0.088 across templates, below the 0.1 good threshold.

checkOutcomes.method: DevTools trace and layout long-task observers
checkOutcomes.evidence: The trace recorded zero long tasks and 0ms total blocking time; Lighthouse TBT was 30ms.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against script/link attributes and Lighthouse
checkOutcomes.evidence: A parser-inserted stylesheet is render-blocking with an estimated 810ms saving; total transfer was 872KB and LCP was slow. Scripts identified by HAR were defer/async.
Lighthouse estimated 382KiB unused JS, including 141KB ad code and 118KB first-party vendor code; 14KiB consent CSS was unused.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audit, image audit, and DOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: An icon-only toggle button has no accessible name, five iframes have no title, and six images lack alt text.
Consent text and controls fail WCAG contrast, with measured ratios from 1.06:1 to 2.8:1.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse heading audit and focus probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The homepage skips from H2 to repeated H4 headings, and focus on the consent dialog has a transparent outline.
Core navigation and score links render around 12px high in a very dense layout, harming scanning and reading comfort.
Many actionable links are far below 44x44 CSS pixels and home/match pages overflow horizontally by 10px.
Lighthouse best-practices scored 1.0 and reported no console-error or uncaught-exception failure.
Doctype and charset are valid, but all seven images omit width/height attributes; six decorative GIFs also lack alt.
The 135KB first-party vendor bundle has no source map, reducing inspector/debugging hygiene.
The calendar page duplicates the generic homepage title and description rather than describing the calendar route.
Viewport metadata is present, but many match links use only scores or a dash as link text, and public detail/table routes declare noindex,nofollow.
Canonical links and 200 responses exist, but robots.txt and sitemap.xml returned 403 to the audit fetch and useful match/standings pages are noindex,nofollow.
No JSON-LD describes sports events or results; og:image incorrectly points to the site root rather than an image.

checkOutcomes.method: headers, cookies, HAR, and secrets audit
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS is used and no secrets were exposed, but CSP/HSTS/nosniff are missing and all five cookies lack Secure and use SameSite=None.
The load contacted 12 third-party origins and four known trackers; 31/41 requests and 692KB/872KB were third-party. The consent text names 210 partners.
No authentication flow or browser permission request exists in the representative public score experience.
checkOutcomes.reason: No authentication flow or browser permission request exists in the representative public score experience.

checkOutcomes.evidence: HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, and CSP frame-ancestors are all absent.

checkOutcomes.method: raw HTML versus rendered DOM discoverability comparison
checkOutcomes.evidence: Homepage raw HTML retains 93% of rendered content words and is not a JS shell; detail raw HTML retains core matchup content although live enrichment lowers coverage to 45%.

checkOutcomes.method: overlay viewport inspection and script attribute probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: The consent overlay remains within mobile and desktop viewports and first-party scripts are deferred rather than parser-blocking.
The site declares display:standalone with install icons and start_url, but has zero service-worker registrations and therefore no offline fallback.
The failure page has an empty title, generic try-later text, and no retry/status detail; it does provide only a homepage link.
The document is lang=en while the mandatory consent UI is Czech; dir is absent and inspected CSS contains no logical inline/block properties.
The English match page hard-codes a 22.07.2026 numeric date while geolocated consent is Czech, with no locale switch or locale-labelled formatting.
Global fixtures show bare times such as 19:00 and 19:30 without a time-zone label or user-zone explanation.

checkOutcomes.method: consent-flow screenshot and DOM copy inspection
checkOutcomes.evidence: A blocking consent wall appears before content and presents extensive processing by 210 partners. Reject is available and equally styled, reducing but not removing the nagging-wall concern.
No user-input form exists in the audited score, detail, standings, calendar, or error paths.
checkOutcomes.reason: No user-input form exists in the audited score, detail, standings, calendar, or error paths.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No address, payment, sign-in, sign-up, or other text-entry form exists in scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: No address, payment, sign-in, sign-up, or other text-entry form exists in scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No account or checkout flow exists; consent provides equally prominent accept/reject buttons and management options, and betting links identify their destination.
All seven images use legacy PNG/GIF formats and omit intrinsic dimensions; six below-fold GIFs are not lazy-loaded, though byte cost is small.
The page transfers an estimated 382KiB of unused JavaScript, much of it advertising and analytics work unrelated to viewing scores.
Third parties account for 31 requests and 692KB, including 257KB ads, 154KB tag manager, 148KB consent tooling, and 84KB fonts.
No declared agent-facing intent, transactional tool surface, WebMCP registration, or agentic form exists; this emerging capability is out of scope.
checkOutcomes.reason: No declared agent-facing intent, transactional tool surface, WebMCP registration, or agentic form exists; this emerging capability is out of scope.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The live-score experience has no summarisation or language-model task for which on-device inference is necessary.
checkOutcomes.reason: The live-score experience has no summarisation or language-model task for which on-device inference is necessary.

checkOutcomes.evidence: This MPA exposes navigation and one-shot consent rather than a representative repeatable same-document interaction; fabricating a loop would not model real use.
checkOutcomes.reason: This MPA exposes navigation and one-shot consent rather than a representative repeatable same-document interaction; fabricating a loop would not model real use.

checkOutcomes.method: heap summary and runtime memory/DOM probe
checkOutcomes.evidence: A simple text-centric results page retained 311,295 heap nodes and 18.65MB self size, with 6,258 DOM elements, 5 iframes, and 1,406 interactive/tabbable nodes.
The heap summary exposed no Detached* constructor among reported constructors; no repeatable same-document interaction existed to provoke listener/timer accumulation.

principleOutcomes.reason: No declared agent-facing intent, transactional tool surface, WebMCP registration, or agentic form exists; this emerging capability is out of scope. The live-score experience has no summarisation or language-model task for which on-device inference is necessary.
